text: If your cat ever knocks on your bedroom door... do not open it.
Do not get up. Do not turn on the light. Do not call out.
It is three in the morning.
This is Instruction four zero four.
There are four rules. Follow them exactly.
Rule one is about the door. Rule two is about the gap under it. Rule three is about your eyes.
Rule four is the emergency protocol. How to fight back.
Break the first three, and rule four is all you have left.
Rule one. Do not open the door.
Listen to where the knock comes from. Not the bottom of the door. The middle.
A cat that wants in will scratch. It will push. It will cry.
It will not knock. Cats do not knock.
This one knocks right in the middle. Where a hand would knock.
If you open the door, it will not come in like a cat. One swipe. Its claws, across your throat. Faster than you can blink.
It does not need you to open the door. It knows how. It only knocks to find out if you are awake.
Rule two. Do not look under the door.
There is a light on in the hallway. You did not leave it on.
In the gap under the door, there are two shadows. A cat stands on four.
Do not count them again. The number will not change.
Then it will meow.
Grown cats almost never meow at each other. The meow is a sound cats made only for people.
You know this meow. You have heard it every morning for years.
But it is too slow. It is too low. And it comes from too high up.
Rule three. Pretend to be asleep.
The knocking will stop. Silence does not mean it left. It always comes in.
You will hear the handle turn. Slowly. It has been practicing.
Close your eyes before the door opens. Not after. It can see an eye closing.
Lie on your side. Breathe slow, and deep. Do not squeeze your eyes shut. It knows the difference.
It will walk to the bed. It will stand over you, and lean down, close to your face.
You will feel its breath on your cheek. It smells like your cat.
It is checking. Do not move. Do not swallow.
If it believes you, it will drop to four legs, and curl up at the foot of the bed. Like it always does.
In the morning, it will be back on the bed. Four legs. Purring.
Look at the door before you leave. Right in the middle.
Three marks. Like claws. Too far apart to be claws.
Rule four. Emergency protocol. How to fight back.
If you closed your eyes too late, and it saw you, the first three rules are over.
Here is what does not work.
Do not throw things at it. It will dodge every one. It has been practicing that since it was a kitten.
Do not run. A house cat can run nearly fifty kilometers an hour. This one has longer legs.
Do not offer it your arm to buy time. It will take the arm. You will not have enough blood left to need it back.
Do not cover yourself in catnip. It will not distract it. You will only taste better.
There is only one thing that works.
Sit up on the bed, like a dog. Look it in the eyes. And bark. Loud.
Do not stop.
It will flatten its ears. It will step back. It will drop to four legs and walk away, as if nothing happened.
Keep barking until the sun comes up. Your neighbors will complain. Let them.
In the morning, your cat will be on the bed, purring. Feed it. Pet it.
Do not mention the barking. It will not mention the knocking.
This was Instruction four zero four.
